title: vz-pipe-new pipesim crashes at lib.js:74 when -c used as --compile
description: Repro: vzpac (or vz-pipe-new) pipesim '...' --fw --asm-ins 5 --is-loop -n 28 -c -s ./assets/sim. Crash: bin/lib/vz-pipe/lib.js:74 _.join(_.map(options.conflicts.split(','), dep), '\n'). Cause: -c short flag collision. bin/vz-pipe-new.js:30 defines -c, --conflicts <string>; shared registerCompileOptions (bin/lib/artifacts.js) also defines -c, --compile. caporal binds -c to --conflicts and consumes -s as its value; dep('-s') then fails. Fix options: (a) drop the -c short on vz-pipe-new's --conflicts (keep long form), or (b) drop -c short on the shared --compile and only expose long form. Prefer (a) — shared option should win across the suite. Acceptance: original command runs to completion with PDF output; --conflicts <string> still usable via long form.
close_reason: Resolved: dropped -c short on --conflicts in bin/vz-pipe.js (bin/vz-pipe-new.js is a symlink to it, so both aliases fixed). Original crash at lib.js:74 no longer reproduces. Note: running the repro command now reveals a separate, pre-existing issue — vz-pipe latexArtifact() calls in bin/lib/vz-pipe/lib.js never received the packages/tikzLibraries backfill from netlistsvg-6qo, so xelatex compile fails with 'Environment tikzpicture undefined'. Tracked separately.

title: vz-pipe-new short flag collision with shared compile options
description: Why: shared registerCompileOptions added -c/--compile across vz-* CLIs (netlistsvg-6qo). vz-pipe-new pre-existed with -c, --conflicts <string> at bin/vz-pipe-new.js:30. Collision means -c on vz-pipe-new pipesim now resolves ambiguously and breaks the command. Scope: resolve flag collision in vz-pipe-new (rename --conflicts short flag) and audit other vz-* CLIs for similar collisions before adopting shared compile options.

title: vz-sched: wakeup/start vrt check uses omega*lambda instead of omega/lambda
description:
In bin/lib/vz-sched/lib.js the preemption check on task start (_start_task, line 96) and wakeup (_wakeup, line 123) computes the woken/new task's effective vrt as:

    tw.vrt + schedule.class.wgup * (tw.lambda / sumlambda())

Per spec (lecture model), the comparison should add omega DIVIDED by the woken task's lambda, i.e.:

    tw.vrt + schedule.class.wgup / tw.lambda

Currently omega is multiplied by lambda (and scaled by sumlambda), giving the wrong preemption decision. Fix both call sites (lines 96 and 123) and update fixtures/snapshots under bin/lib/vz-sched/__snapshots__/ accordingly.
acceptance_criteria:
- _start_task uses wgup / lambda for the comparison
- _wakeup uses wgup / lambda for v and tw.vrtlwk strings
- Snapshots regenerated and tests pass (node bin/test.js / vz-sched suite)
close_reason: Implemented as part of netlistsvg-3l0.1: _start_task (lib.js:96) and _wakeup (lib.js:123) now use the shared wakeupV(tw) = tw.vrt + omega / tw.lambda helper. Snapshots regenerated. ADR 0001 decision #1.

title: vz-cache sim --compile fails: missing amssymb/xcolor in preamble
description: Repro: vz-cache.js sim '0.1,1.1,1.0,1.1' --simplesim 1011111001,1,0110101011,0 -c -x ./ese0 -b 9 -s 11 -m 20 -w 1. Error: xelatex fails on ese0-complete-trace.tex (and likely ese0-blank-trace.tex). Cause: trace artifacts use \checkmark (amssymb) and \color (xcolor); only declared in addoptions for tikz2pdf, not as packages for wrapTex. Fix: pass packages array to all five vz-cache latexArtifact() calls (badge/cache-data*: probably none beyond default; complete-trace: [amssymb, xcolor]; blank-trace: [amssymb]). Acceptance: repro emits all 5 PDFs.
close_reason: Added packages=['amssymb','xcolor'] to both trace artifacts in bin/vz-cache.js. Verified: repro emits all 5 PDFs.

title: artifacts: extend latexArtifact w/ packages+tikzLibraries and add xelatex+pdfcrop compile path
description:
Two coupled changes in bin/lib/artifacts.js + per-tool call sites + per-tool CLI:

1. Extend latexArtifact signature:
   latexArtifact(code, name, clss, engine, addoptions, packages=[], tikzLibraries=[])
   - 'packages' = LaTeX \usepackage list (e.g. ['karnaugh-map','tikz','longtable','amsmath'])
   - 'tikzLibraries' = \usetikzlibrary list (e.g. ['matrix','chains','calc'])
   - Both default to []. Backward compatible with existing call sites.

2. Add a new compile path that mirrors pac/exam-sheets/assets.mk:
   compileArtifactsXelatex(data, pfx, opts)
   For each artifact, write a .tmp.tex of shape:
     \documentclass[a4paper,landscape]{article}
     \usepackage{fontspec}
     \setmainfont{<font>}
     \usepackage[margin=.5cm]{geometry}
     \usepackage{<pkg>}        # for each packages[]
     \usetikzlibrary{<lib>}    # for each tikzLibraries[]
     \pagestyle{empty}
     \begin{document}
     <code>
     \end{document}
   Run: xelatex -interaction=nonstopmode -shell-escape <tmp>
   Run: pdfcrop <pfx>-<sfx>.pdf <pfx>-<sfx>.pdf
   Cleanup .tmp.*, *.aux, *.log, _minted*.
   opts.font defaults to 'Minion Pro' (matches assets.mk); override via CLI.

3. Update each tool's CLI (sched, quine, cache, mmu, memmap, rv-fcall, wave, fsm, pipe, netlist, nomnom, compile-artifacts) to expose:
     -c, --compile           emit PDFs via compileArtifactsXelatex instead of .tex
     --font <name>           override default 'Minion Pro'
   When neither --save nor --compile is given, keep current default (dump JSON or save tex per tool).

4. Backfill packages/tikzLibraries at known call sites by reading pac/exam-sheets/20260218/q-*/makefile:
     - vz-quine artifacts: ['karnaugh-map','tikz','longtable','amsmath']
     - vz-rv-fcall artifacts: packages ['tikz','minted']; tikzLibraries ['matrix','chains','calc']
     - vz-sched artifacts (rt diagram, data table, wakeup conditions): ['tikz','amsmath']; tikzLibraries ['arrows']
     - vz-wave artifacts: keep existing addoptions (already pass -i preamble) for compatibility, also add packages ['ifthen']; tikzLibraries ['patterns']
     - vz-pipe artifacts: read bin/preambles/pipe.tex to derive needed packages
   For tools whose preamble is already injected via addoptions (wave/pipe), be careful not to double-include.

Acceptance:
  - latexArtifact accepts the new optional args (existing 5-arg calls unchanged)
  - compileArtifactsXelatex produces PDFs matching what assets.mk would have produced (visual diff on q-1.1 fc-* and q-2.3 rv-fun-*)
  - 'vz-quine -s ./fc "x00010x10x00111x" -r a,b,c,d --compile' emits ./fc-*.pdf
  - 'vz-rv-fcall artifact rv-fun-spec.json -s rv-fun --compile' emits rv-fun-*.pdf
  - existing tests pass
acceptance_criteria:
- latexArtifact extended with packages, tikzLibraries
- compileArtifactsXelatex implemented in bin/lib/artifacts.js
- --compile / --font flags wired in all relevant vz-* tools
- per-tool call sites carry the right packages/tikzLibraries lists
- visual equivalence vs assets.mk for q-1.1 and q-2.3 sample sheets
close_reason: Implemented in bin/lib/artifacts.js: latexArtifact extended with optional 'packages' and 'tikzLibraries' args; new compileArtifactsXelatex builds the same preamble as pac/exam-sheets/assets.mk (fontspec + geometry + \usepackage + \usetikzlibrary) and runs xelatex+pdfcrop entirely in a tmp dir via tmp-promise (unsafeCleanup) so only the cropped <pfx>-<sfx>.pdf lands in cwd — no .tex, .aux, .log, _minted* leftovers. Added writeArtifacts dispatcher and addCompileOptions helper. Wired '-c/--compile' and '--font' on sched, quine, fsm, cache, mmu, wave, pipe pipesim, rv-fcall artifact. Packages backfilled for quine (tikz, longtable, amsmath; karnaugh-map for kmap), rv-fcall (tikz; minted for source listings; matrix/chains/calc), sched (tikz, amsmath, amssymb; arrows/positioning). Backward compatible: --save still emits .tex. Smoke-tested 'vz-quine ... --compile' end-to-end: 7 PDFs produced, no other files in cwd. vz-sched + vz-pipe jest 43/43 pass. No new lint errors.

title: vzpac: implement dispatcher binary with subcommands (drop prefix, shim old bins)
description:
Create bin/vzpac.js as the single Caporal-based dispatcher. Each existing vz-* tool becomes a subcommand with the vz- prefix dropped.

Subcommands (initial):
  vzpac netlist            (was vz-netlist)
  vzpac sched              (was vz-sched)
  vzpac pipe               (was vz-pipe / vz-pipe-new — same module)
  vzpac cache              (was vz-cache.js)
  vzpac mmu                (was vz-mmu)
  vzpac memmap             (was vz-memmap)
  vzpac fsm                (was vz-fsm)
  vzpac quine              (was vz-quine)
  vzpac wave               (was vz-wave)
  vzpac spim               (was vz-spim)
  vzpac rv-fcall           (was vz-rv-fcall)
  vzpac nomnom             (was vz-nomnom)
  vzpac compile-artifacts  (was vz-compile-artifacts)

Implementation:
  - Refactor each bin/vz-*.js to expose its Caporal program (or main(args) function) instead of immediately calling .parse(process.argv). The vzpac dispatcher imports them and registers them as subcommands via prog.command('<name>', '<desc>').action(...).
  - Old bin/vz-*.js scripts become thin shims: just  so existing scripts/users keep working.
  - Update package.json bin map: add 'vzpac', keep all existing vz-* entries pointing at their (now-shim) files.

Acceptance:
  - 'vzpac --help' lists all subcommands with short descriptions
  - 'vzpac sched --help' shows the same help as 'vz-sched --help' did
  - Each old vz-* binary still works and produces identical output for at least one existing fixture per tool (golden test)
  - Tests (bin/test.js, bin/testbatches.js, bin/testcache.sh, jest suites) still pass
acceptance_criteria:
- bin/vzpac.js created and registered in package.json
- All 13 subcommands wired and reachable via 'vzpac <name>'
- All old vz-* bin entries still work as shims (backward compatible)
- All existing tests pass without changes
close_reason: Implemented in-place register pattern: each bin/vz-*.js exports register(prog) and runs standalone via SUBNAME injection (if require.main === module). bin/vzpac.js requires all 13 modules and assembles the unified caporal program. package.json: added 'vzpac' entry; vz-* entries unchanged (work as standalone shims via the in-file standalone wrapper). 'vzpac --help' lists all subcommands. Lint: 0 new errors. vz-sched + vz-pipe jest: 43/43 pass. bin/test.js (vz-cache shell tests) pre-existing 22 failures unchanged. Smoke-tested: 'vzpac cache sim' and 'vz-cache.js sim' produce identical output.

title: vz-sched: add printConditions LaTeX artifact for vrt-update conditions on wakeup/start
description:
Add a new generator function printConditions(history, schedule) in bin/lib/vz-sched/lib.js that emits a LaTeX itemize/aligned block listing, for every wakeup AND every task start in the run history, the conditions used to update the woken/new task's virtual runtime and the preemption comparison against the currently active task.

For each event the block should show:
  - task name (woken/started) and timestamp
  - tw.vrt before clamp
  - clamp: tw.vrt = max(tw.vrt, vmin - latency/2)
  - effective comparison value v = tw.vrt + omega / tw.lambda  (per netlistsvg-yr5.1 fix)
  - state.curr.vrt at the moment of comparison
  - decision: preempt (checkmark) or not (times)

Wire it into saveIt() in lib.js as an additional latexArtifact entry (name e.g. 'wakeup conditions', standalone/pdflatex/-r varwidth) so it is saved alongside the rt-diagram and data-table artifacts. Update fixtures/snapshots accordingly.

Implementation notes:
  - The simplest source of truth is to capture structured wakeup/start records inside _wakeup and _start_task (push to e.g. history.conditions = [{kind, time, task, vrtBefore, vrtAfter, v, currVrt, decision}, ...]) rather than re-parsing tw.vrtlwk strings.
  - Reuse the same omega/lambda formula as the (fixed) preemption check to avoid drift.
acceptance_criteria:
- New printConditions function in bin/lib/vz-sched/lib.js
- Covers both _wakeup and _start_task events
- saveIt() emits the new artifact alongside existing ones
- Snapshots regenerated; vz-sched tests pass
- LaTeX renders cleanly via standalone/pdflatex
notes: Decision: implement with canonical omega/lambda formula already in place (ADR 0001). yr5.1 reduces to migrating existing _start_task/_wakeup call sites to the shared helper.
close_reason: Implemented: shared wakeupV helper (canonical omega/lambda per ADR 0001), state.conditions capture in _start_task and _wakeup, printConditions LaTeX generator wired into saveIt as 4th artifact ('wakeup conditions'). Tests pass (5/5 vz-sched, snapshots regenerated).

title: vz-sched artifacts & presentation

title: vz-sched: verify state.vmin excludes waking task's rho during wakeup
description:
In bin/lib/vz-sched/lib.js, _wakeup (line 118) reads state.vmin at line 120 to clamp the waking task's vrt:

    tw.vrt = Math.max(tw.vrt, state.vmin - schedule.class.latency / 2);

state.vmin is recomputed in _task_tick (line 154) as _.minBy(state.rbt, 'vrt').vrt. At the moment of the read on line 120 tw is still in 'blocked', so vmin does not yet include tw — but after addToRbt(tw) on line 122 the next vmin refresh will include tw.vrt, which can pull vmin down if the waking task carried a stale/low rho.

Per spec, when a task wakes up, state.vmin must not consider the rho of the waking task itself. Investigate whether:
  - vmin needs to be refreshed inside _wakeup BEFORE the clamp on line 120 (using rbt excluding tw — currently safe since tw isn't in rbt yet, but worth confirming the read isn't stale from a prior tick),
  - and/or whether subsequent vmin updates should explicitly exclude just-woken tasks for some interval.
acceptance_criteria:
- Document the expected invariant for vmin around wakeup
- If broken, fix vmin computation/refresh so the waking task's rho is excluded as required
- Snapshots regenerated and vz-sched tests pass
close_reason: Verified during 3l0.1 implementation: in _wakeup, state.vmin is read before addToRbt(tw), so tw is still in 'blocked' and structurally excluded from rbt-based vmin (mirrors Linux place_entity pre-enqueue read). Documented in code comment ('ADR 0001, decision #2') at the clamp site.
